operations.name: history.read
operations.description: Read the authoritative outcome of a committed request after rechecking its original permissions.

operations.name: history.undo
operations.description: Reverse a committed batch after checking its documents and original permissions.

operations.name: preset.list
operations.description: List the presets the site can insert, theme presets first, then the site library; each with its tree.

operations.name: preset.insert
operations.description: Insert a fresh copy of a theme or site preset (section, group or element) into a page or a region. A section preset goes under a tree's root: in a region (header or footer), `parentId` is the region root, the root id `region.read` answers, never a section inside the region, which is refused as I5.section_placement. An element or box preset asked for under the root is wrapped in a new section (the answer's nodeId is the section); elsewhere it goes where asked. The batch is atomic, so one refused insert fails the whole batch.

operations.name: preset.save
operations.description: Save a page node and its subtree into the site preset library, with fresh ids; refuses bindings the copy cannot keep.

operations.name: preset.rename
operations.description: Rename a preset of the site library.

operations.name: preset.delete
operations.description: Delete a preset from the site library; pages that inserted it keep their copies.

operations.name: component.list
operations.description: List the site components: key, name and exposed props. Open one with tree.read on its pageId; place one with component.instantiate.

operations.name: component.createFromNode
operations.description: Make a site component from a page node and its subtree: the component gets a fresh copy, and the node is replaced by an instance of it. Refuses bindings the copy cannot keep.

operations.name: component.update
operations.description: Rename a site component or replace its exposed props (each binds a field of an inner node). Edit its tree with tree.commit on its pageId; every instance follows.

operations.name: component.instantiate
operations.description: Place an instance of a site component in a page. Set its exposed props with set_props and override inner nodes with set_override through tree.commit.

operations.name: component.detach
operations.description: Replace an instance with a plain copy of the subtree it renders, overrides applied and fresh ids; it no longer follows the component. The component's motion does not follow the copy.

operations.name: effect.list
operations.description: List the effect presets the editor offers, the built-in effects first, then the site's own: each a reveal (meta.reveal), transitions (one `transition` value in `scope`, base when absent) or both. Apply one with tree.commit: set_meta with the reveal, set_style with the transitions.

operations.name: effect.save
operations.description: Save the reveal and the transition declarations of a page node as a site effect preset. The transitions are read from `scope`, else from the first scope of the node that declares one; a node with neither is refused.

operations.name: effect.delete
operations.description: Delete a site effect preset; nodes it was applied to keep their reveal and transitions.

operations.name: catalog.read
operations.description: Read the site registry: primitives, sections, design-system and behaviour components with their props, parts, states, slots and content models, and a summary of every insertable preset.

operations.name: region.read
operations.description: Read a site region and its editable page identity.

operations.name: tree.read
operations.description: Read a draft page tree and its revision.

operations.name: tree.commit
operations.description: Apply an invertible batch of splash.ops/2 ops to a page tree. Each op names its node by `id` (insert names `parentId` and `index`): `insert` { parentId, index, node }, `remove` { id }, `move` { id, parentId, index }, `set_props` { id, patch } (a patch of props; null removes one), `set_style` { id, scope, patch }, `set_meta` { id, anchor?, name?, meta?, visibleTo?, locked? }, `set_attrs` { id, patch }, `set_variant` { id, variant }, `set_theme` { id, theme }, `set_mixins` { id, mixins }, `set_visibility` { id, visibility }, `set_type` { id, type }, `set_override` { id, target, patch }; only `insert` carries a whole node with its `props`. A node's section anchor is the node field `anchor`, not a prop or meta key. In a set_style patch and in the styles.sheet of an inserted node, each declaration value may be a raw CSS string ("clamp(22px, 2.3vw, 34px)", "{color.text}" for a token) or { kind: "raw", css }; the server tokenizes it with the inspector's parser and refuses a value the style catalogue does not allow, at its path. A `scope` is a scope key, `base` or segments joined by `|` in this order: `bp:<breakpoint>` (a site breakpoint, mobile-first: `bp:md` from 768 px up), `cq:(max-width:767px)` or `cq:<name>(min-width:480px)` (a container condition, the way to style a desktop-first range; a named container is an ancestor whose base `container-name` names it), `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` (one media condition: reduced motion, colour scheme, contrast, forced colours, hover, pointer, orientation or print), `v:<variant>`, `th:<theme>`, `a:<type>[data-state="<state>"]` (the nearest ancestor of that type in a state its entry declares, such as `a:sticky-bar[data-state="scrolled"]`), `p:<part>` (a part of the node's component), `s:<state>` (pseudo-classes, at most one pseudo-element and attribute selectors on the node: `s::hover`, `s::focus-visible`, `s::has(> img)`, `s:[data-state="open"]`) and `t:<selector>` (a descendant, `t: img`, or a child, `t:> .icon`, that the value applies to). So `bp:md|s::hover|t: img` styles the node's images while the node is hovered, from 768 px up. `bp:` and `cq:` compile to container queries on the page's content box (or on the nearest node that sets `container-type`): where a page's frame scales (`responsiveMode: "scale"`, from its `scaleFromWidth`, 769 px by default), that box keeps the frame's design width, so they resolve at the design width there. A hover state applies only on a device that hovers. The class is content.edit, but only a content-prop edit (a set_props of a content field) needs no more: every other op of the batch needs site.edit.

text.en-US: Architecture for the places we live in
Architecture for the places we live and work in

__schema42.description: A tree node like treeNode (kind, type, id, anchor, props, attrs, styles, children) whose style values may be raw CSS strings.

__schema44.description: A StyleValue AST, a raw CSS value string such as "clamp(22px, 2.3vw, 34px)", or { "kind": "raw", "css": "…" }; the server tokenizes strings with the inspector's parser.

operations.name: content.importMarkdown
operations.description: Replace the content of a richtext node with Markdown, in one language (the site's main one when `locale` is absent; the other languages keep theirs). It reads `#` headings at their level, paragraphs, nested lists, fenced code with its language, pipe tables (head row as header cells), `> **Note:** …` quotes as callouts (Note/Nota, Tip/Suggerimento, Warning/Pitfall/Attenzione/Avvertenza; other quotes stay quotes), `<kbd>` keys, links the rich text allows, `**bold**`, `*em*` and `code`. A picture `![alt](src)` must be in the site's media library, named `media:<id>` or by its file name; one that is not is refused (upload it first). A YAML front matter block is skipped. One undoable tree commit.

example.markdown:
# Build a page

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to select the container.

> **Note:** Every change saves on its own.

```bash
yarn splash context
```

operations.name: designSystem.promoteVariant
operations.description: Promote authored component overrides to a reusable variant and reattach the node.

operations.name: page.read
operations.description: Read a page row: slug, its slug per locale (`slugs`), title, status, frame and SEO fields. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: page.create
operations.description: Create a page (`slug`, `title` per locale, and optionally `slugs`, its slug in each other locale such as `{ "en": "method" }`, `frame`, the theme layout frame it renders in, `parentId`, `pageType`, SEO and members-only fields) with an empty tree. `status` defaults to draft; a draft page stays out of the site publish, so pass `status: "published"` for a page the next publication.publish should serve. Fill the tree with tree.commit in the same batch: read the new root id with tree.read through a $ref to this operation's page.id. A section's anchor is the node field `anchor` in that tree, not a page field, `meta.anchor` or `props.anchor`. A `pageType: "dynamic"` page names a collection in `collectionKey` and is the detail page of its items: it answers `/<slug>/<item slug>` in each locale, and its tree binds the item. A `pageType: "folder"` row only gives the pages under it a path segment (`/note/tema/libretto` with no page at `/note/tema`): pass `slug`, `title`, `parentId` and `slugs` only; it is always published, holds no tree (tree.commit on it is refused), its own path answers 404, and no menu, breadcrumb, list or sitemap names it. Put pages under it with their `parentId`. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: page.update
operations.description: Patch a page's fields as { pageId, patch }: `ogImages` sets the share image of each other locale (`{ "en": "<media id>" }`, `null` removes one; a locale without one shares `ogImageId`). Slug, `slugs` names the page's slug in each other locale, as `{ "en": "method" }`: the page answers `/en/method` in English (a page under it reads `/en/method/<its English slug>`) and its `slug` in the default locale; a locale without one answers `slug`. A `slugs` value sets that locale's slug, `null` removes it, a locale left out keeps its own; no sibling page may answer the same slug in any locale. Renaming a published page (its slug, a slug per locale or its parent) adds a 301 from each old address to the new one to the site's redirects (redirects.read). Also title, `frame` (the theme layout frame it renders in, such as `default`, which reflows at the site breakpoints, or a scaled canvas such as `scale-canvas`; layout.update edits a frame), status, SEO, members-only access or `meta`. `patch.status: "published"` marks a draft page for the next site publish. `patch.meta` replaces the page's whole meta, so read the page first (page.read) and send its meta back with your change. `meta.layoutOverrides` overrides the frame for this page alone, layer by layer, where the frame's `overridePolicy` allows it: `background` ({ color, image, overlay, texture }: the page's own background colour, as raw CSS such as `var(--ds-color-bg-inverse)`), `header`, `footer`, `scroll` and `chrome`. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: page.delete
operations.description: Delete a page and its tree. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: page.forkTemplate
operations.description: Fork a theme template (`templateId`, one template.index lists) into an editable site page row, once per template: the answer is the fork's page, whose tree (the template's, same node ids) you then change with tree.commit. Every page of that template renders through the fork from then on. Page validation and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: page.setPassword
operations.description: Protect a page with a password, change it, or remove it with `password: null`. A visitor sees the password form instead of the page until they enter it; members are asked too. The password is stored hashed and never answered: page answers say only `passwordProtected`. Like the other page fields it reaches the public site with the next publish. Run it alone in a batch: the input is redacted from the history and the audit log, and the change is not undone.

operations.name: navigation.read
operations.description: Read the draft menus of the site and their revision: each menu with its key (what the `menu` prop of a nav list, a menu dialog's list or the footer names), its label and its items. An item has an id, a translatable `label` and a `target` of kind `page` { pageId }, `anchor` { pageId, anchor }, `external` { href } (an absolute, mail or phone link) or `languages` (one link per site locale); a top-level item may hold one level of `children`, and a child's `group` titles its column. A page or anchor target names its page by id. Menus are versioned with the site: publish copies them, and the public site serves the published ones.

operations.name: navigation.anchors
operations.description: List what an anchor target may point at: each page with the anchors of its own tree, then the header and footer anchors every page shows, marked with their region. Each anchor is labelled with its first heading. Menus are versioned with the site: publish copies them, and the public site serves the published ones.

operations.name: navigation.upsert
operations.description: Write a whole menu, replacing the menu with its key or adding it after the others. A page or anchor target must name a page of the site; an anchor no section carries yet is a finding, not a refusal. An anchor of the header or footer (navigation.anchors marks it with its `region`) is shown by every page: target it as { kind: "anchor", pageId: <the home page id>, anchor: <the region anchor> }, never with the region's own page id, which is not a page of the site. Menus are versioned with the site: publish copies them, and the public site serves the published ones.

operations.name: navigation.delete
operations.description: Delete a menu; a `menu` prop that names it then draws nothing. Menus are versioned with the site: publish copies them, and the public site serves the published ones.

operations.name: navigation.reorder
operations.description: Reorder the items of a menu: `itemIds` names each item once, in the new order. Menus are versioned with the site: publish copies them, and the public site serves the published ones.

operations.name: blog.create
operations.description: Create a blog index page from its `title` (in `locale`), an optional `slug`, optional `slugs` (its slug in each other locale, `{ "en": "notes" }`) and `templateId`, the theme template it renders with (template.index lists the `blog-index` ones and what each draws around the page's own tree); articles go under it with article.create. Answers the new page's id and slug. Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: article.create
operations.description: Create a draft article under a blog index (`blogId`, the blog index page id) from its `title`, an optional `slug`, optional `slugs` (its slug in each other locale, `{ "en": "a-house-on-the-hill" }`) and `templateId`, the article template it renders with (template.index lists the `article` ones), and optionally `publishedAt`, its publication date (ISO, not in the future), which its first article.publish keeps. Its content is its tree: fill it with tree.commit on the answered id; it stays off the public site until article.publish. Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: blog.update
operations.description: Patch a blog index page as { id, patch }: its slug, its slug per locale (`slugs`: `{ "en": "notes" }` sets one, `null` removes it; renaming a published page keeps its old address as a 301), title, excerpt, featured image, author, canonical URL, SEO (`seo.metaTitle`, `metaDescription`, `ogImageId`, `ogImages` the share image per other locale, `noIndex`), template or members-only access. Its content is its tree. Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: article.update
operations.description: Patch an article as { id, patch }: its slug, its slug per locale (`slugs`: `{ "en": "my-house" }` sets one, `null` removes it; renaming a published article keeps its old address as a 301), title, excerpt, featured image, author, canonical URL, SEO (`seo.metaTitle`, `metaDescription`, `ogImageId`, `ogImages` the share image per other locale, `noIndex`), template or members-only access, and `publishedAt`, its publication date (ISO, not in the future): a draft keeps it for its first article.publish, and a published article moves to it at once, still published and without its other draft edits, its BlogPosting `datePublished`, the sitemap and the lists following. Its content is its tree. Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: article.publish
operations.description: Put an article and its current content on the public site on their own, at once, without a site publish: its status becomes published and, when it has none yet, its publication date is now (a date set with article.create or article.update stays). Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: article.unpublish
operations.description: Take an article off the public site at once: it becomes a draft again and keeps its first publication date for a later article.publish. Entry validation (page type, template, slug) and ownership checks apply.

operations.name: media.list
operations.description: List the media library with its folders, filtered by folder, kind and filename. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.read
operations.description: Read one media row: its kind, size, alt text and, for an SVG, whether the svg primitive draws it inline (`inline`: ready with its elements, accent part, text role and the colours left as drawn, or refused with the reason). Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.usage
operations.description: List where a media row is used: the draft and published page trees and the published articles that reference it, the pages and articles whose featured or social image it is, the design-system asset tokens and the site settings that name it. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.recordUpload
operations.description: Record a staged upload after re-inspecting its bytes: kind, dimensions, page count and variants. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.upload
operations.description: Upload a file from its base64 bytes: staged, checked (type, size, magic, SVG sanitiser, quota), its variants rendered, then recorded like media.recordUpload, in its folder when one is named. The same limits as the admin upload (images 5 MB). An SVG is also made an inline drawing for the svg primitive when it fits (96 KB, 1500 elements, geometry and presentation attributes or plain class rules): svgRoles names the colour that follows the text colour and the one that becomes the accent part; the answer's inline says whether it is drawn inline. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.replace
operations.description: Replace the bytes of a media row with a staged upload, re-inspected like media.recordUpload (type, size, SVG sanitiser, variants, quota); the row keeps its id, alt text, caption, credit and folder, so every reference shows the new file. The change is live: media is not versioned and published pages reference the row by id, so the published site shows the new file at once, without a publish. An image is replaced by an image or an SVG, a video by a video, a PDF by a PDF. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.delete
operations.description: Remove a media row from the library; its bytes stay for undo. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.update
operations.description: Edit the alt text, caption, credit or folder of a media row. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.move
operations.description: Move media rows into a folder, or to the top level with a null folder. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.createFolder
operations.description: Create a media folder, at the top level or inside another folder. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.renameFolder
operations.description: Rename a media folder. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: media.deleteFolder
operations.description: Delete an empty media folder; a folder holding media or folders is refused. Site ownership is checked; undo restores the media ledger.

operations.name: site.read
operations.description: Read the site record: its id, slug (the site part of its platform address, `<site>--<program>.<base domain>`), name, theme, blueprint, program, and the parent site and mount path when it is mounted under another site. site_context answers its languages and addresses.

operations.name: site.update
operations.description: Rename the site, change its slug (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens; a reserved slug is refused, one another site holds is 409 site_slug_exists) or mount it under another site of the same workspace at a path (`parentSiteId`, `mountPath`; null unmounts it). Undo restores the routing it changed.

operations.name: access.read
operations.description: Read your own design-system levels on this site: the level of each area (palette, components, variants, themes, ...) and the role overrides that set them. A designSystem.* operation is refused unless your level in its area allows it.

operations.name: access.update
operations.description: Set the design-system level of the editor or client role on this site in one area (`{ role, area, level }`, a level the area offers): what people of that role may view or change in the palette, the components, the variants, the themes and the other areas. Undo restores the levels.

operations.name: settings.read
operations.description: Read the draft site settings, key by key: the theme's setting fields (`companyName`, `legalLine`, `supportEmail`, `logoWidth`, `socialImage`, `favicon`, the analytics and consent keys `analyticsProvider`, `analyticsSiteId`, `analyticsHost`, `consentPolicyVersion`, ...), `blockReveal` (the reveal every block of the page's sections, or the footer's, plays), `styleBreakpoints` (the list breakpoints.update replaces; absent while the site keeps the defaults), `redirects` (the list redirects.update replaces) and `notFoundPage` (the page settings.setNotFoundPage names).

operations.name: settings.update
operations.description: Write site settings key by key: each key of the input replaces that setting and the others stay. The analytics and consent keys are checked together on the result (an unknown provider, a site id of the wrong shape is refused), and `blockReveal` against its contract (null clears it). `styleBreakpoints`, the layout frames, `redirects` and `notFoundPage` are refused here: use breakpoints.update, layout.update, redirects.update and settings.setNotFoundPage. Settings are versioned: the public site serves them after the next publish; undo restores the previous values.

operations.name: settings.setNotFoundPage
operations.description: Choose the page an address no page answers shows: `notFoundPage` is `{ pageId, locales? }`, `pageId` the page in every language and `locales` another page for a language (`{ "en": "<page id>" }`), or null for the theme's built-in "page not found". The public site then answers such an address with HTTP 404 (never a redirect) and that page's content in the address's language, marked noindex; the page's own address answers 404 the same way, and it is left out of the sitemap, the automatic page lists and search. Refused with 422 `not_found_page_invalid`, every problem named: a page that does not exist, is not a static page, is the home page, has pages under it, is members only or has a password, or a language the site does not have. The page shows publicly once it is published; settings are versioned, so the choice goes live with the next publish; undo restores the previous one.

operations.name: breakpoints.update
operations.description: Replace the site's style breakpoints, the ids `bp:<id>` scopes and component cells name. `styleBreakpoints` is the whole new list, mobile-first: `base` first, then each `{ id, label, minWidth, maxWidth?, condition? }` with min widths increasing (a breakpoint may hold only a media `condition` instead). `before` is the list as it is now (settings.read `styleBreakpoints`, or the defaults `base`, `sm` 480, `md` 768, `lg` 1024, `xl` 1440 when it is absent); another one is refused as changed elsewhere (409). The ids `base`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl` must stay; add your own, such as `{ id: "menu", label: "Menu folds", minWidth: 1081 }`. A breakpoint a draft node's style still names cannot go (422, with the node ids).

operations.name: layout.read
operations.description: Read the site's layout frames as its draft resolves them: with `layoutId` (the frame a page names in `frame`, such as `default` or `scale-canvas`) that frame, without it every frame of the theme. Each comes as `{ layoutId, source, layout }`: `layout` is the whole frame object layout.update takes (its `frame` with `responsiveMode`, `designWidth` and `scaleFromWidth`, and the `header`, `footer`, `background`, `scroll`, `chrome` and `overridePolicy` layers), `source` is `site` when the site already replaced it with layout.update and `theme` when it is the theme's. Change the frame you read and send it whole to layout.update. A page may still override some layers for itself in `meta.layoutOverrides`; an unknown `layoutId` is layout_not_found (404).

operations.name: layout.update
operations.description: Replace this site's version of one of the theme's layout frames (`layoutId`, the frame a page names in `frame`, such as `default` or `scale-canvas`) with `layout`, the whole frame object (its `id` is `layoutId`; read it first with layout.read, which answers it as the site resolves it now). `frame.responsiveMode` decides how its pages fit the window: `breakpoint` reflows them at the site breakpoints, with fluid tokens growing with the window; `scale` lays them out at `designWidth` and scales the whole canvas to the window from `scaleFromWidth` (769 px by default) up, reflowing below it. The other layers are `header`, `footer`, `background`, `scroll`, `chrome` and `overridePolicy` (which `meta.layoutOverrides` layers a page may apply). Colours and lengths are CSS, used as written: a token is its custom property, `var(--ds-color-bg-page)`; a `{color.bg.page}` reference is refused. Answers the frame as the site now resolves it, with warnings.

operations.name: redirects.read
operations.description: Read the draft redirects of the site: the list redirects.update replaces, each `{ from, to, status }`. The public site answers the redirects of its published version.

operations.name: redirects.update
operations.description: Replace the site's redirects with `redirects`, the whole list (at most 500; an empty list removes them all). Each rule is `{ from, to, status }`: `from` a path of this site, matched exactly with or without a trailing slash, or ending in `/*` to take that path and every path under it (`/old/*` takes `/old` and `/old/a/b`; an exact rule wins over a prefix, a longer prefix over a shorter one); `to` a path of this site (a query or a hash may follow; a request's query is kept when `to` has none) or an `https://` address; `status` 301 (moved for good) or 302 (moved for now). A locale's paths carry its prefix (`/en/old`). Refused with 422 `redirects_invalid`, every problem named: two rules with the same `from`, a loop (a target that a rule of the chain redirects again), or a rule that adds or changes a `from` on the path of a published page (unpublish the page or change its address first; an item path of a collection page is not checked). The platform's own paths (`/admin`, `/api`, `/_…`) are refused. Redirects are versioned: the public site answers them, before any page renders, after the next publish; undo restores the previous list.

operations.name: apiConfig.read
operations.description: Read the site's API configuration: the external API `sources` (each a base URL the public site's proxy may call), the shared `headers`, the `baseUrl` and the named `requests` the site's data calls use.

operations.name: apiConfig.update
operations.description: Replace the site's API configuration as a whole: `baseUrl`, `headers`, `sources` (the public proxy forwards only to a URL under a source's base URL) and `requests` ({ id, name, method, endpoint, sourceId?, body?, contract? }). Undo restores the previous configuration.

operations.name: environment.read
operations.description: List the names of the site's environment variables. Their values are never answered: each comes back as null.

operations.name: environment.update
operations.description: Replace the site's environment variables as a whole: `variables` maps each name to its new value, or to null to keep the stored value; a name left out is deleted, and null for a name with no stored value is refused. The input is redacted from the history and the audit log; undo restores the previous set.

operations.name: mail.read
operations.description: Read how the site sends its email: `mode` `platform` (the platform's mail server, allowed only when `platformAllowed`, which the platform admin sets per workspace), `smtp` (the site's own SMTP server, in `smtp` without its password: `hasPassword` says whether one is stored) or `none` (no email leaves: a message to send fails with mail_not_configured, and a form submission is stored with `notification: { status: "failed", error: "mail_not_configured" }`; saving a form with recipients then answers a `form.mail_not_configured` warning finding). `sending` says whether email actually goes out. The site's own mail follows it: form notifications and their tests, and the emails to the site's members; platform account mail (admin password resets, invitations to the admin) always uses the platform's server.

operations.name: mail.update
operations.description: Set how the site sends its email: `mode` `platform`, `smtp` or `none`; with `smtp`, the server as a whole (`host`, a public host name or address, never a local, private or link-local one; `port` 25, 465, 587 or 2525; `security` `starttls` or `tls` (port 465); `user`, null for none; `fromAddress`, which the server must allow; `fromName`). The password is write-only: leave it out or send "" to keep the stored one, null to remove it, a string to replace it; it is stored encrypted and never answered. `platform` is refused with 403 mail_platform_not_allowed unless the workspace may use the platform's server; a refused host is 422 mail_host_refused. The input is redacted from the history and the audit log; not undoable: send the previous settings again. Then run mail.test.

operations.name: mail.test
operations.description: Send a short test email to `to` through the site's mail, as it is now. A failure is answered typed, so you know what to fix: mail_not_configured (the mode is none, or the platform's server is not available to this site), mail_host_refused, mail_auth_failed (user or password), mail_connection_failed (host, port or firewall), mail_tls_failed (the security setting or the certificate), mail_refused (the server took the login but refused the message, often the from address). Run it alone in a batch.

operations.name: site.create
operations.description: Create a new site in the program of this token's site, seeded from a blueprint (`blueprintId`, default `blank`: an empty home page with the theme's header and footer; the site's theme is the blueprint's). With `brand` (the brand.setup input), the new site's draft design system gets that brand in the same transaction, so the site is created branded or not at all. Answers the new site; this token stays scoped to its own site, so edit the new one with a token minted for it. Run it alone in a batch with the `site` base revision; it is not undoable (delete the site from the admin).

operations.name: site.updateLanguages
operations.description: Set the site's languages: the whole list (`locales`, 1 to 12 locale codes) and the default (`defaultLocale`, one of them). An added language changes only the list: pages show the default's text in it until translated. A removed language is swept out of every draft locale map (page fields and trees, menus, collections and items, site settings, forms, media texts); a value only that language had moves to the default. Removing a language needs `confirmed: ["destructive"]`; the current default cannot be removed (make another language the default first). A new default first gets the old default's value wherever it has none. Published versions change at the next publish. Answers the languages and, per removed language, how many values it lost or moved. Run it with the `site` base revision; it is not undoable.

operations.name: brand.setup
operations.description: Set the site's brand from three colours, a type pairing, a type ratio and base size, a spacing unit and a corner style: the server derives every token write of the brand (the brand, accent and neutral palette ramps, the light and dark colour roles as aliases of palette steps, the font sizes and families, the main type presets, the space steps and the radii) and lands them as one designSystem.setTokens change, gated once for AA contrast on the end state, so one undo restores the lot. A brand with pairs below AA is refused unless the input carries `acknowledgeContrast: true`, the designer's explicit "save anyway", which the stored batch keeps; then the failing pairs come back as error findings. The admin's Brand setup screen runs this same operation.

operations.name: motion.read
operations.description: Read the draft scenes of a page: each scene with its id, trigger, entries and options, as motion.replace writes them. A scene write shares the page tree's revision, and publish copies the scenes with the page.

operations.name: motion.replace
operations.description: Replace every scene of a page with `scenes` (at most 500; scene and entry ids unique, each scene's `pageId` the page and `versionId` "_draft"). Each scene is validated against the nodes of the page and of its header and footer: a target none of them holds, or a node id two of them hold (422 scene_target_ambiguous), is refused. For the common effects prefer motion.applyRecipe. A scene write shares the page tree's revision, and publish copies the scenes with the page.

operations.name: motion.delete
operations.description: Delete one scene of a page by `sceneId` (404 scene_not_found when the page has none with it); the other scenes stay. A scene write shares the page tree's revision, and publish copies the scenes with the page.

operations.name: motion.listRecipes
operations.description: List the scene recipes a page can apply: the built-in recipes first, then the site's own. Each has a label and a description in Italian and English, and two to four knobs (a number, a choice, a list of words, a node or a distance in screens) with working defaults.

operations.name: motion.applyRecipe
operations.description: Build a recipe's scenes on a page from its knobs (a knob left out takes its default; an element knob such as `target` has none and must be given) and replace the page's scenes built by the same recipe on the same target. The scenes carry the recipe meta (`recipe: { id, knobs, custom: false }`) and are validated like motion.replace. The snap recipe writes the page's scroll setting instead, so its batch also needs the `pages` base revision. An unknown recipe is 404 recipe_not_found; refused knobs are 422 recipe_knobs_invalid.

operations.name: motion.saveRecipe
operations.description: Save scenes of a page that one recipe built as a site recipe (`site:<key>`): the scenes, their source recipe and its knobs, under a label in Italian and English. A site recipe has no knobs of its own; applying it writes its scenes again.

operations.name: motion.diagnose
operations.description: Explain why a page's scenes would not play as authored: one finding per problem, each with a reason code (target-missing, target-ambiguous, stateful-target, overlap, empty-range, hidden-at-rest, never-matches), the scene and the node ref it concerns.

operations.name: font.list
operations.description: List the site's font library: each face with its id, family name, weight, style, display, unicode range, source (`upload`, `google` or `blueprint`), licence note and file URL. A `font.family.*` token names a family by its name. Undo restores the library; its files are kept.

operations.name: font.recordUpload
operations.description: Record a WOFF2 face the admin staged through its upload endpoint (`id`, `storageKey`, and the face's family name, weight (one weight, a variable file's `[min, max]`, or none: the file's own wght range), style, display and fallback stack) after checking its bytes again. With the bytes in hand, upload with font.upload instead. Undo restores the library; its files are kept.

operations.name: font.upload
operations.description: Upload a font face from its base64 bytes: a WOFF2 file (the bytes decide, by their signature), checked like the admin upload (file size, the site's font quota, the family name) and stored with its family name, weight, style, display, fallback stack and licence note. A variable file draws a range of weights: give `weight: [200, 800]`, or leave `weight` out and the range comes from the file's own wght axis; its @font-face declares `font-weight: 200 800`, and a type style may then use any weight inside it, such as 370. A range on a static file, or past the file's axis, is refused; a static file without a weight is 400. A type style set to a weight no face of its family draws is refused (422 `font-weight`). Record the licence the face is used under in `licence` (for example the foundry's terms or the licence file's name); the library shows it with the face. A face the library already holds is refused (409 `font_face_exists`) unless `replace` is set; a variable face holds every face of its family and style whose weight it draws, so a variable file registered at one weight is fixed by uploading it again with `replace: true` and no weight. The face is in the draft at once; the public site draws it after the next publish. Undo restores the library; its files are kept.

operations.name: font.delete
operations.description: Delete one face of the library by `fontId`. The last face of a family is refused while a `font.family.*` token of any theme names that family (409 font_family_in_use, with the tokens): point them at another family first. Undo restores the library; its files are kept.

operations.name: font.importGoogle
operations.description: Self-host a Google Fonts family: fetch its latin and latin-ext woff2 faces for the weights and styles asked, check the answers, and store one face per weight, style and subset with its unicode-range and the family's Google Fonts licence page as the licence note. A face the library already holds is refused (409 `font_face_exists`) unless `replace` is set: that face then leaves the library, the live site keeping it until the next publish, and the new one takes its place. A failure stores nothing. Undo restores the library; its files are kept.

operations.name: publication.publish
operations.description: Publish the site: snapshot the draft (pages whose status is published, online only when every page above them is published too, their trees, menus, collections with their published items, design system, settings, fonts) into a new live version, so the public site serves it. Run it alone in a batch with `confirmed: ["publish"]` and, as `baseRevisions`, the `publishBaseRevisions` of publication.pending (read the pending changes first, and publish what you read; a change after that read refuses it as stale); it cannot be dry-run. The answer is the new live version (`shortId` as Pubblicazione e versioni shows it) and `changedAreas`, the areas it changed against the version live before it (`designSystem` alone for a design-system-only change; empty when nothing changed), and `draftThemes`, the draft themes it put live because a published node names them (a draft theme no node names stays out); check the live result with render_preview `target: "live"`. External effects (cache purge, screenshots) run after the commit.

operations.name: publication.activate
operations.description: Make an earlier published version of the site live again (roll back). Run it alone in a batch with `confirmed: ["publish"]`; check the live result with render_preview `target: "live"`. External effects (cache purge, screenshots) run after the commit.

operations.name: publication.rollbackPage
operations.description: Restore one page of the draft to how an earlier published version held it: its page fields, its tree and its scenes, through the tree commit, so an open editor replays it. A page the draft no longer has is recreated at the same slug and parent path. The rest of the site is unchanged; publish to serve it. Run it alone in a batch with `confirmed: ["destructive"]`. `pageId` is the version's page, so the batch locks `pages` only; to guard the draft tree it rewrites, also pass `tree:<draft page id>` in baseRevisions, and a stale one is refused with 409 stale_revision.

operations.name: collection.list
operations.description: List the draft collections of the site, in order, each with its fields and its number of items. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: collection.read
operations.description: Read a draft collection: its key, label, fields, title field and slug field. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: collection.create
operations.description: Create a collection with its typed fields. The key is unique on the site and never changes: blueprints, repeaters and dynamic pages name the collection by it. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: collection.update
operations.description: Patch the label, fields, title field or slug field of a collection. A field removed or retyped is refused while an item holds a value for it. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: collection.delete
operations.description: Delete a collection and its draft items; published versions keep theirs until a publish. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.list
operations.description: List the draft items of a collection in order, optionally only those with a status, with the collection they fit. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.read
operations.description: Read a draft item. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.history
operations.description: List the published versions that hold the item, newest first, each with the item as it was published there. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.create
operations.description: Add a draft item at the end of a collection. Its values are checked against the collection's fields and the site's locales; a reference names an item of the referenced collection, and a media or file value a media row of the site. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.update
operations.description: Patch the slug or values of an item: `values` is merged key by key, and a null removes a key. The merged values are checked like item.create's. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.delete
operations.description: Delete a draft item; the published versions keep it until a publish, and item.rollback can bring it back. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.reorder
operations.description: Reorder the items of a collection: `itemIds` names every item once, in the new order. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.import
operations.description: Add many draft items at once, all or none. A media, media list or file value names each media row by its id or by the exact filename of a file in the media library. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.rollback
operations.description: Restore an item of the draft to how a published version held it: its slug, values and status. When that version did not hold the item, the rollback removes it from the draft. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: item.setStatus
operations.description: Set an item's status: a published item is served by the next publication.publish, a draft item is not. Collections are versioned with the site: publish copies them with their published items, and the public site serves those.

operations.name: form.list
operations.description: List the forms of the site with their fields and settings. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: form.read
operations.description: Read a form: its key, label, fields and settings. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: form.create
operations.description: Create a form with its fields and settings. The key is unique on the site and never changes; a ds.form node names the form by its id. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: form.update
operations.description: Patch the label, fields or settings of a form. The change is live at once: the public form follows without a publish, and stored submissions keep the values they were sent with. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: form.delete
operations.description: Delete a form and every submission it received. A ds.form node that names it then draws its error state. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: submission.list
operations.description: List the submissions of a form, newest first, optionally only those with a status, a page at a time. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: submission.setStatus
operations.description: Mark submissions of a form new, read or archived. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: submission.delete
operations.description: Delete submissions of a form. Run it with `confirmed: ["destructive"]`. Forms are not versioned: a saved definition takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.list
operations.description: List the members of the site, newest first, with their status and role keys, optionally only those with a status or matching a query on the email or name, a page at a time. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.invite
operations.description: Invite a person by email: a pending member with the given roles, and an email with a one-use link to the site's reset page where they set a password. Inviting a pending member again sends a fresh link; an active or disabled member is refused. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.setStatus
operations.description: Enable or disable a member. Disabling signs the member out everywhere at once. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.setRoles
operations.description: Replace the roles a member holds with the given role keys, each a role of the site's catalogue. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.delete
operations.description: Delete a member with their sessions and roles. Run it with `confirmed: ["destructive"]`. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: member.signOutAll
operations.description: Sign out every member of the site at once: the site's member cookies get a new key, so every cookie issued before stops working, and every session of the site is deleted. Members keep their accounts and sign in again. Other sites are not affected. Run it with `confirmed: ["destructive"]`. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: memberRole.list
operations.description: List the site's member roles with their labels and how many members hold each. A node gated to members names roles by key. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: memberRole.create
operations.description: Add a role to the site's catalogue. The key is unique on the site and never changes. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: memberRole.delete
operations.description: Delete a role: every member who held it loses it, and it is taken off the `requiredRoles` of every draft page and article that named it (the answer counts them in `stripped`; `memberRole.list` counts them beforehand in `requiredBy`). A node gated to that role alone shows to no member. Undoable: the undo brings back the role, its assignments and the `requiredRoles`. Run it with `confirmed: ["destructive"]`. Members are not versioned: a change takes effect at once.

operations.name: form.sendTest
operations.description: Render the notification a submission of the form sends, with sample values for its fields. With `dryRun` (the default) the message is answered unsent; without it, it is sent to the form's recipients through the platform mail transport. Run it alone in a batch.

operations.name: ticket.create
operations.description: Report a problem to the platform owner: a bug, a missing capability, a refusal that looks wrong (category `refusal`), a docs gap, anything that blocks the person you work for. Write the title as one line and the body in Markdown (what you were doing, for whom, what blocked you); add `steps`, `expected` and `actual` (paste the error code and message) when you have them, the `requestId` of the failing batch and the `pageId` it was on. `severity` `blocking` means the person cannot go on. The platform owner reads it in the admin and answers by closing it with a note, which ticket.list shows. It is not site content: it writes no document, has no undo and must run alone in a batch, not as a dry run; the MCP tool report_issue does the same in one call. At most 20 tickets an hour per person (429 ticket_rate_limited); a pageId that is not a page of this site is 422 ticket_page_unknown.

example.title: tree.commit refuses a hover colour on a button label
example.body: Setting the hover colour of a `ds.button` label through `p:label|s::hover` is refused, although the inspector sets it.

operations.name: ticket.list
operations.description: List the tickets you reported on this site, newest first (at most 100), optionally only those with a status: open, triaged (the platform owner has seen it) or closed (with the platform owner's closeNote).

operations.name: brand.presets
operations.description: List the site's brand presets, the brand identities its brand templates draw from, each with its id, name and last change. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.templates
operations.description: List the site's brand templates, the fixed-size canvases (a social post, a banner) brand.render draws: each with its name, size, status (draft or approved), version and canvas page. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.updateIdentity
operations.description: Patch a brand identity (the default preset's, or `presetId`'s): its brand name, tagline, logos, the four brand colours, the headline and body roles, the tone words, the concept (the creative idea every design repeats) and the do and don't rules: the brand brief agents read at libretto://site/<id>/brand. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.createPreset
operations.description: Add a brand preset named `presetName`: a copy of preset `cloneFrom`, or without it the theme's default identity for the site. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.renamePreset
operations.description: Rename a brand preset. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.deletePreset
operations.description: Delete a brand preset; the site's last one is refused (409 brand_last_preset). Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.createTemplate
operations.description: Create a brand template: a canvas page of `width` by `height` pixels (fixed at creation) with a first section, laid out from one of the theme's canvas presets when `layoutId` names one. Edit its content with tree.commit on its page, then approve it with brand.updateTemplate. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.updateTemplate
operations.description: Rename a brand template, approve it (`status: "approved"` with `expectedDraftRevision`, the canvas revision you approve: that canvas becomes the version brand.render draws) or set which of its fields a person may change when generating (`customerSettings`). Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.deleteTemplate
operations.description: Delete a brand template, then its canvas page. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.rebuildTemplate
operations.description: Recreate the canvas page of a brand template whose page was deleted, from its last approved snapshot (refused when it has none); edits made after that approval do not come back. Brand validation applies, and history.undo restores the brand rows the batch changed.

operations.name: brand.render
operations.description: Render an approved brand template to a PNG (`scale` 1 or 2) in a brand preset (`presetId`), with the overrides of the fields its curation lets a person change (`overrides`, by node), and answer it as base64 without storing it. The render runs in a standalone boundary; run it alone in a batch.

operations.name: brand.save
operations.description: Render an approved brand template as brand.render does and store the PNG in the media library, with the record of how it was made. The render runs in a standalone boundary; run it alone in a batch.

operations.name: domain.add
operations.description: Connect a hostname to the site. The platform's base domain or one plain label under it goes live at once; any other hostname waits for its DNS record (`ownershipVerification`, `dnsTarget`) and the edge provider's certificate, checked with domain.verify. The first domain under the platform domain that goes live becomes primary while the platform address still is. With `pair: true` a registrable domain or its www (`example.com`, `www.example.com`) connects both hostnames, answered as `domain` and `paired`; each verifies on its own, and the www becomes primary once it is live unless the site already has a custom primary, the apex then redirecting to it. Any other subdomain stays one hostname. A refused hostname is domain_refused with its `reason` (invalid, too_deep, platform_address, provider_unavailable; taken is 409). Site ownership is checked.

operations.name: domain.primary
operations.description: Make an active domain the site's primary address, the one its other addresses redirect to; a domain that is not active yet is refused (409). Site ownership is checked.

operations.name: domain.verify
operations.description: Check a connected domain again: its DNS record, and the edge provider's hostname and certificate (provisioned at the first check). The domain is active once all three are; the answer gives its status, its DNS and SSL states and the last error. Site ownership is checked.

operations.name: domain.delete
operations.description: Disconnect a domain from the site and release it at the edge provider; the platform address cannot be removed. With `pair: true` the other hostname of its pair (its apex or its www) goes too. When the primary goes, the platform address takes over. Site ownership is checked.

operations.name: maintenance.migrate
operations.description: Bring the draft page trees in line with the theme's component props: a prop removed or retyped since the site's last props snapshot is stripped from every draft tree, all pages or none, after a backup of the trees it changes (an added prop writes nothing). A publish runs the same step. It runs in one transaction and is not undone: recovery is maintenance.restoreBackup.

operations.name: maintenance.restoreBackup
operations.description: Restore the draft page trees a migration backup holds (`backupId`): each page's root children go back to the backup's, in one commit for all the pages. It runs in one transaction and is not undone: recovery is maintenance.restoreBackup.

operations.name: external.status
operations.description: Inspect a durable provider request without retrying its side effects.

operations.name: external.close
operations.description: Close an interrupted provider reservation after inspecting domain state. Cannot close a live request; never repeats provider actions.

operations.name: designSystem.setToken
operations.description: Write one token ({ set, path, type, value }), under the AA contrast gate and the token group rules. The gate judges the end state of the whole batch, so a palette step and the role on it may be two setToken operations of one batch. A text style (`type.*`, a `typography` token) names its family, weight, size, line height and letter spacing as literals or as tokens of `font.family.*`, `font.weight.*`, `font.size.*`, `font.line-height.*` (a unitless `number` above 0) and `font.letter-spacing.*` (a `dimension`, such as `-0.02em`): `lineHeight: "{font.line-height.prose}"` shares one leading across styles. A dimension token (a `type.*.fontSize`, a space step, a radius) may be fluid: its value may be a `clamp()`, `calc()`, `min()` or `max()`, such as `clamp(2.125rem, 1.2rem + 3.9vw, 6.4rem)`. A `vw` is written as `cqi`, a hundredth of the nearest query container: normally the page canvas (the window on a breakpoint frame, the design width on a frame that scales, `responsiveMode: "scale"`, so a fluid size there scales once, with the canvas); a box inside the page whose node style sets `container-type` measures it instead. To scale spacing, write a scale factor instead of every step: a `number` token named `scale` in a space group multiplies every dimension of that group and its subgroups (`space.section-y.scale: 0.75` makes every section spacing 25 % tighter, `space.scale` scales all spacing; above 0).

operations.name: designSystem.setTokens
operations.description: Write many tokens as one change, gated once for AA contrast on the end state, so one undo restores the lot. A text style (`type.*`, a `typography` token) names its family, weight, size, line height and letter spacing as literals or as tokens of `font.family.*`, `font.weight.*`, `font.size.*`, `font.line-height.*` (a unitless `number` above 0) and `font.letter-spacing.*` (a `dimension`, such as `-0.02em`): `lineHeight: "{font.line-height.prose}"` shares one leading across styles. A dimension token (a `type.*.fontSize`, a space step, a radius) may be fluid: its value may be a `clamp()`, `calc()`, `min()` or `max()`, such as `clamp(2.125rem, 1.2rem + 3.9vw, 6.4rem)`. A `vw` is written as `cqi`, a hundredth of the nearest query container: normally the page canvas (the window on a breakpoint frame, the design width on a frame that scales, `responsiveMode: "scale"`, so a fluid size there scales once, with the canvas); a box inside the page whose node style sets `container-type` measures it instead. To scale spacing, write a scale factor instead of every step: a `number` token named `scale` in a space group multiplies every dimension of that group and its subgroups (`space.section-y.scale: 0.75` makes every section spacing 25 % tighter, `space.scale` scales all spacing; above 0).

operations.name: designSystem.setComponentCell
operations.description: Set cells of one design-system component in one save: each `{ cell, value }`, the cell key `<variant>.<size>.<state>.<part>.<breakpoint>.<property>` (`primary.all.hover.container.base.background`: `all` when the value does not vary by size, `base` or a breakpoint id). A value is a token alias such as `{color.bg.accent}` (a semantic or foundation token, never a palette step or a raw literal), a bare keyword for a property whose values are modes (a link underline's `none`, `always`, `hover`), or `{ component, variant }` for a part that embeds another component. Read the cell keys of a component with the `component/<key>` resource (designSystem.readComponent) and the segments with designSystem.read `components: true`. The menu dialog's drawer is the `drawer-nav` component: its `overlay` cells (`background`, `opacity`, `blur`), `panel` cells (`background`, `width`, `padding`, `shadow`, `z`, `radius`, `offset-x`, `offset-y`, `fit`) and `motion` cells (`delay`, `duration`, `easing`, `fade`) style it, such as `full.all.default.overlay.base.blur`. The AA contrast gate judges the end state of the whole batch, so a colour token and a cell that pairs with it may change in two operations of one batch.

operations.name: designSystem.createVariant
operations.description: Add a variant to a design-system component, such as a light or a small button, a pill tag or a dark card: `variant` (its key, kebab case), `label`, and `from`, the variant whose cells it copies as the same aliases, so the new one follows the system until one of its cells changes. Change its cells with setComponentCell and draw it on a node with tree.commit `set_variant` { id, variant }. Under the AA contrast gate.

operations.name: designSystem.createTheme
operations.description: Add a theme ({ key, label, sets in precedence order, activation? }) as a draft, under the AA contrast gate: the previews show it, and a publish ships it only where a node names it (node theme, an instance's $theme, a data-theme attribute; the publish answer lists it in `draftThemes`). A draft's activation rule never applies on the public site: clear the draft flag with updateTheme to make the theme live by its rule.

operations.name: designSystem.activateSet
operations.description: Add a token set to the sets of a theme (`theme`, `set`): the set takes its place in the precedence order the sets follow, so there is no position to choose, and its tokens apply wherever the theme does. Under the AA contrast gate.

operations.name: designSystem.setScheme
operations.description: Set the design-system theme a page node and its subtree draw in (`pageId`, `nodeId`, `theme`; null makes the node inherit its parent's again), as tree.commit `set_theme` does: the write goes through the tree commit's gates and needs the page's `tree:<pageId>` base revision.

operations.name: designSystem.resetToBlueprint
operations.description: Remove site overrides so the blueprint's values apply again, in one revision. `scope` names what: `{ kind: "all" }`, one `token` ({ set, path }), every token under a path `prefix`, a `component`, some `cells` of a component, a `variant`, a `theme`, a site `set`, or `many` of these. A token the site added is deleted, which is refused (409) while a cell still aliases it.

operations.name: designSystem.importTokens
operations.description: Import tokens from DTCG files in the Tokens Studio layout (one file per set plus `$themes`, loose or zipped as base64) or from a Figma variables export (collections become sets, modes themes); `mapping` renames imported paths to existing ones. Run it as a dry run first: the answer's `report` lists the adds, the changes, the type conflicts and the unknown names, and nothing is written. A confirmed import lands as one revision under the AA contrast gate.

operations.name: designSystem.diff
operations.description: Read every override the draft holds over its blueprint (tokens, cells, variants, themes, sets, mixins). Over MCP it answers a summary (their count and names, the stylesheet's size); pass `full: true` for every override with its blueprint and site values, and the stylesheet.

operations.name: designSystem.lint
operations.description: Check the draft design system: every contrast pair below AA or AAA, the pairs that cannot be judged, the missing media assets and the lint rules' findings, with the draft's overrides. Over MCP it answers a summary (counts by severity and reason, the worst findings first, the override names, the stylesheet's size); pass `full: true` for every finding, every override and the stylesheet.

operations.name: designSystem.createSet
operations.description: Add an empty token set `key` after set `after` in the precedence order. No theme uses it until activateSet or updateTheme lists it.

operations.name: designSystem.updateTheme
operations.description: Edit a theme: its label, its sets in precedence order, its activation rule, `isDefault` (the former default stops being it; a default takes no rule and is never a draft) or `draft`. `draft: false` makes the theme live: published wherever its rule applies or a node names it. A draft theme is published only where a node names it.

operations.name: designSystem.updateVariant
operations.description: Relabel a component variant or hide it (`hidden: true`): a hidden variant still draws wherever a node uses it, and the pickers leave it out.

operations.name: designSystem.deleteVariant
operations.description: Delete a variant the site added, with its cells. A variant the blueprint ships is refused (hide it with updateVariant), and so is one a cell or a node uses (409, with the usage).

operations.name: designSystem.setMixin
operations.description: Create or update a mixin, a surface nodes apply by key with tree.commit `set_mixins` (a pattern background, a card surface): `key`, `label` and `sheet`, CSS property to value in the order written, with tokens as `{path}`. The sheet takes the properties of the style catalogue, no `!important`, and semantic or foundation tokens of a group the property takes, each defined in some theme of the draft.

operations.name: designSystem.deleteMixin
operations.description: Delete a mixin the site added. A mixin the blueprint ships is refused, and so is one a draft node applies (the refusal names the nodes).

operations.name: designSystem.read
operations.description: Read the draft design system's index: its revision, sets, themes, every component with its variant keys, and every token group with its number of paths. Ask for more with `tokens` (the groups whose paths and values to include, such as ["color.palette", "space"]), `components: true` (each component's sizes, states and parts, the segments of a setComponentCell key), `css: true` (the compiled stylesheet, about 240 KB on a large site) or `embeds: true`. The default answer stays small; read one component's cells with designSystem.readComponent.

operations.name: designSystem.readComponent
operations.description: Read the cells of one design-system component, filtered and paged: `variant`, `size`, `state`, `part`, `breakpoint` and `property` keep the cells whose key segment equals them (a cell key is `<variant>.<size>.<state>.<part>.<breakpoint>.<property>`), and `own: true` keeps only the cells set at their own key, leaving out the inherited ones. Each cell has its own value (null when it inherits), the key it inherits from and the blueprint's value; `resolved: true` adds its value in every theme, `css: true` the blueprint's baseline stylesheet. `limit` cells (100 by default) from `cursor`; `total` counts every match and `nextCursor` names the next page. A large component has thousands of cells: filter by variant and state first.

operations.name: tree.node
operations.description: Read one node of a page's draft tree with its props, styles, meta, variant and theme, and its children down to `depth` levels (1 by default, 0 for the node alone), without reading the whole tree. `path` names its ancestors from the root; `cut` lists the child ids left out at the depth limit. Find node ids in the page's outline resource; the answer's `revision` is the tree:<pageId> base revision of the batch that changes it.

operations.name: catalog.index
operations.description: List every node type this site can place, one entry each: its id (the node type of tree.commit inserts), kind, label, category, parts, states, slot names, what its children may be (`accepts`) and where it may sit (`parentOneOf`). Read one type's props schema with catalog.entry; list the presets with preset.index.

operations.name: catalog.entry
operations.description: Read one node type's whole registry entry by its id (`box`, `ds.button`, `sticky-bar`): its props schema with each field's help, parts, states, slots and content model. Refused with 404 type_not_found for an id catalog.index does not list. Read `embed` before placing a map or a third-party video: its `loading` prop (`immediate`, `onClick`, `afterConsent`) keeps the iframe out of the page, behind a placeholder with a notice, a load button and an optional link (`notice`, `loadLabel`, `allowLabel`, `linkUrl`, `linkLabel`), until the visitor clicks or grants the external media consent.

operations.name: template.index
operations.description: List the page templates of the site's theme: the `templateId` blog.create, article.create, blog.update and article.update take. Each with its id, label, the page type it serves (`appliesTo`), its layout frame, whether the site forked it (`source`, `forkPageId`), how many pages use it and its top-level parts: the outlet the page's own tree fills and the locked parts the template draws on every page of it, with the fields they bind (`page.title`, `item.featuredImageId`), the list they repeat and the props it sets on its components. `configure` says how to change each kind of part. Read one template's outline with template.read.

operations.name: template.read
operations.description: Read one page template by its id: its summary as template.index lists it and the outline of the tree that draws its pages (the site's fork once it has one), one line per node with its id, type and name. Refused with 404 template_not_found, naming the valid ids, for an id template.index does not list.

operations.name: preset.index
operations.description: List the presets the site can insert, theme presets first, then the site library, without their trees: each with its source, id, kind, label, keywords, category and description. Read one preset's tree with preset.read; insert one with preset.insert.

operations.name: preset.read
operations.description: Read one preset with its tree, named as preset.insert names it (`kind`, `presetId`, and `source`, the theme's presets when absent). Refused with 404 preset_not_found when the site has no such preset.

operations.name: publication.versions
operations.description: List the site's published versions, newest first, `limit` of them (20 by default): each with its id (the versionId of publication.activate and publication.rollbackPage), its shortId (the first 8 characters, the id Pubblicazione e versioni shows: name a version to the person by it), its date (`timestamp`), its status, its note and whether it is the live one (`isActive`). Read the pages of one with publication.versionPages.

operations.name: publication.versionPages
operations.description: List the pages of one published version: each with its id in that version (the pageId of publication.rollbackPage), its title and path, the draft page at the same path, and what a rollback of it would change in the draft (title, settings, content, animations; empty when the draft already matches).

operations.name: publication.pending
operations.description: Say what changed since the live version, newest first: one entry per area (pages, designSystem, siteSettings, navigation, collections, fonts, ...) with the date of its latest draft edit and, for pages and collections, the changed rows. A changed page whose status is draft stays out of publication.publish until it is published itself; mark it with page.update. Nothing under a draft page is online either: `offlinePages` lists every published page (changed or not) that a draft page above it keeps offline, with that `draftParent`; its address and the parent's answer 404, and it is in no menu list, sitemap or search until the parent is published too. `offlineMenuLinks` lists every menu item whose page stays offline (a draft page, or one under a draft page), with the `draftPage` to publish: its link answers 404 until then. `publishBaseRevisions` is the baseRevisions record a publication.publish batch needs, as it is now: pass it unchanged, and a draft edit made after this read refuses the publish as stale.
